key_insight: Detonation-sprayed titanium dioxide-based coatings can have their roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity tuned by adjusting spraying parameters, especially nozzle speed and spray distance.
engineering_relevance: The study provides practical process–property relationships and predictive equations that can help optimize coating production for surfaces requiring controlled wettability and morphology.
method: Varied detonation spraying process conditions for titanium-based metal-ceramic coatings.
Measured surface roughness, coating thickness, and hydrophobicity/contact angle.
Fit empirical laws linking nozzle speed and spray distance to surface response.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that roughness and thickness follow an inverse power law with nozzle passage speed, while roughness and contact angle follow a parabolic dependence on spray distance.
watch_item: The conclusions appear to rely on empirical process fitting, so the equations may need validation for other materials, substrates, or equipment setups.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
